thread.title: Ciscomani introduces bill amending Sikes Act for land management near military bases
thread.title_full: Ciscomani introduces bill amending Sikes Act for land management near military bases

author: Tucson Standard
title: Ciscomani introduces bill amending Sikes Act for land management near military bases
text:
Juan Ciscomani, U.S. Representative for Arizona's 6th Congressional District | ciscomani.house.gov
Juan Ciscomani, U.S. Representative for Arizona's 6th Congressional District | ciscomani.house.gov
U.S. Representative Juan Ciscomani has introduced a bill intended to improve the management of lands around military installations, focusing on both operational readiness and environmental stewardship.
The proposed legislation seeks to amend the Sikes Act, originally enacted in 1960, which allows the Department of Defense to work with federal, state, and local organizations on natural resource management for military lands. The amendment would expand the use of cooperative agreements under the Sikes Act to cover not only current or anticipated military activities but also broader operations at military and state-owned National Guard installations. This change aims to give defense agencies more flexibility in managing off-installation lands important for training, environmental resilience, species conservation, and public safety.
Ciscomani said, “This commonsense update ensures that our military installations, including Fort Huachuca, have the tools they need to protect surrounding lands while staying mission-ready. It’s about improving flexibility, enhancing coordination with local and state partners, and supporting conservation without compromising national security.”
Support for the bill comes from local officials and advocacy groups. Sierra Vista Mayor Clea McCaa stated: “The City of Sierra Vista strongly supports H.R. 4293, which strengthens the Sikes Act while balancing the need for military readiness with environmental stewardship. Without this critical amendment, the City’s economic development plans remain vulnerable to legal actions from external special interest groups that allege Fort Huachuca’s operations negatively impact off-post habitat. This bill represents a thoughtful and balanced approach, and the City is grateful for Rep. Ciscomani’s leadership and commitment to our region’s economic and national security.”
Dr. Randy Groth, president of Huachuca 50—a group advocating for Fort Huachuca—said: “The Huachuca 50 supports Rep. Ciscomani’s efforts to amend the Sikes Act through H.R. 4293. For over 20 years, special interest groups from outside Cochise County have targeted Fort Huachuca and the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service with lawsuits, threatening the Fort’s critical role in national defense. This legislation provides a common-sense update that maintains environmental protections while safeguarding military readiness and the local economy. We commend Rep. Ciscomani for his dedication to protecting Cochise County and the nation’s defense capabilities.”
Juan Ciscomani is currently serving as U.S. Representative for Arizona's 6th district after replacing Ann Kirkpatrick in 2023.
In recent elections, Ciscomani won against Kirsten Engel in both 2022 (with a narrow margin) and again in 2024.
